newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Prods Outlook-Gasoline seen steady on demand.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Prods Outlook-Gasoline seen steady on demand.

text.p: Strong demand for U.S. spot gasoline should keep prices from eroding this week, while distillates are likely to remain under pressure.
Traders said gasoline production issues, such as refinery outages, would be a more important factor than the week-to-week statistics on offtake.
"It's not the demand side of the question that's going to change. The supply side is the question," one East Coast market watcher said.
"Gasoline has probably been underperforming for the last two months," the source said. "I expect gasoline to outperform crude and heating oil."

Refineries continued to operate at very strong levels -- 96.8% percent of capacity, according to American Petroleum Institute -- though crude oil has been fairly resistant to bullish trends. As a result, any market strength is likely to be led by gasoline prices."
"Demand for crude oil in the U.S. can't go up, the only possibility is a decline," according to the market watcher.
NEW YORK HARBOR
Gasoline prices are likely to continue their bullish trend for the near term, but distillates will probably remain under pressure because of the strong refinery output and modest seasonal demand.
Prompt conventional M2 gasoline jumped to 59.73 cents a gallon on July 17, the highest price since the beginning of June, before pulling back slightly.
Harbor traders said premium grade gasolines should remain tight this week given the steady demand and lack of nearby barrels.
Much of the tightness was in the reformulated gasolines, traders said, which surged higher last week as the gasoline additive MTBE (methyl tertiary butyl ether) became increasingly scarce.

"MTBE is the big variable," since the tightness in nearby supplies of the gasoline additive forced producers to scramble to meet their needs, the trader said. "Blenders can't afford to make those incremental barrels."

Prompt premium D2 reformulated gasoline differentials gained about 4.0 cents a gallon to peak at 12.00 cents over the August NYMEX last week, while regular A2 reformulated gasoline differentials gained about a cent.
Prompt A2 gasoline barrels were bid at about 1.60 cents over the August NYMEX early Monday, about 0.10 cent up from late Friday levels.
U.S. GULF

Expectations for nearterm direction in the gasoline differentials in the U.S. Gulf Coast appeared mixed, with one trader calling for prompt conventional gasoline differentials to firm early this week, ahead of Wednesday's scheduling deadline on the Colonial Pipeline for the back 21st cycle.
Differentials were then likely to weaken, players said.

"It will probably move in and then move out. We did the same last week," said a trader. Colonial scheduling deadlines have forced differentials sharply higher during recent weeks as traders holding short positions moved to cover at the last minute.
Market players also said tight supplies on reformulated gasoline would likely keep the pressure on A1-grade gasoline differentials in the coming week
In addition, one trader said the driving season has probably not yet peaked, and that the demand for motor fuel was likely to firm differentials in the U.S. Gulf Coast as well as in New York Harbor.
"Premium gasoline usually takes off this time of year and I expect a 9 to 10-cent range with conventional to hold for at least for the week," said the trader.
-- New York Energy Desk +1 212 859 1620
